apod.explanation: The large stellar association cataloged as NGC 206 is nestled within the dusty arms of the neighboring Andromeda galaxy along with the galaxy's pinkish star-forming regions. Also known as M31, the spiral galaxy is a mere 2.5 million light-years away. NGC 206 is found at the center of this sharp and detailed close-up of the southwestern extent of Andromeda's disk. The bright, blue stars of NGC 206 indicate its youth. In fact, its youngest massive stars are less than 10 million years old. Much larger than the open or galactic clusters of young stars in the disk of our Milky Way galaxy, NGC 206 spans about 4,000 light-years.
apod.title: NGC 206 and the Star Clouds of Andromeda

breaking.fact: Producer prices rose 0.3% in October, below the 0.4% forecast and a sharp slowdown from September's upwardly revised 1.4% jump, but the annual rate climbed to 6.5%, the largest in four years, keeping a December Fed rate hike fully priced. Goods rose 0.5%, led by food and basic organic chemicals, while services rose 0.2% for a fifth straight month; core PPI also rose 0.3%.
breaking.headline: October PPI rises 0.3%, below forecast, but annual rate hits a four-year high

breaking.fact: Reuters reported Thursday that Jensen Huang had an intimate relationship with a third Nvidia employee, after the New York Times reported affairs with a former Megaspeed executive US officials suspect of spying for China and with Nvidia health-care chief Kimberly Powell. Huang has agreed to testify before Congress about his interactions with the alleged spy by Thanksgiving, and Singapore said it questioned the Megaspeed executive and seized her passport last year. Nvidia shares, down 4.3% Thursday to $166.19, were up about 1.8% premarket Friday; earnings are due Nov 17.
breaking.headline: Huang to testify before Congress as third affair reported; Nvidia steadies premarket

breaking.fact: Cerebras shares surged about 18% in premarket trading Friday after the AI chipmaker posted a surprise adjusted profit and raised its full-year revenue forecast to $940–960 million; core revenue jumped 70% to $230.9 million, with cloud and services revenue up 265% to about $145 million, and the company signed a cloud deal with Microsoft. The rally would add nearly $4 billion in market value; shares are still down about 47% from their May IPO price of $185.
breaking.headline: Cerebras surges 18% premarket on Q3 beat, cloud boom and Microsoft deal

breaking.fact: President Trump wrote on Truth Social Thursday that the United States does not need a deal with Iran — 'We've got their money, Hundreds of Billions of Dollars, and we've got their Strait!' — and said he had asked Vice President JD Vance, who led the US side of the talks, to turn to corruption in Democratic-run states. Brent rose more than 1% after the post, and traders marked down the odds of a deal by year-end; separately, the IAEA said Friday it cannot locate Iran's Isfahan enrichment plant, calling it a proliferation concern.
breaking.headline: Trump says US needs no Iran deal, pulls Vance off the talks

items.body: Iran's Revolutionary Guards Navy said Friday that a tanker carrying liquefied gas struck a naval mine and suffered an explosion in the Strait of Hormuz while using what Tehran calls an unauthorised and dangerous route. No vessel name, flag, owner or crew details were available, and there was no independent confirmation; reports differed on whether the cargo was liquefied natural gas or liquefied petroleum gas. The claim follows Thursday's reports of four oil tankers hit in the strait.
items.headline: Gas carrier hit by mine in the Strait, Iran says

items.body: Iran's military said Thursday that four oil tankers have now been hit by explosions in the Strait of Hormuz: two supertankers carrying more than 4 million barrels combined were disabled late Wednesday after what Iran calls an unauthorised southern route — Iranian state media said they hit naval mines — and Iran's army said two more tankers hit mines Thursday afternoon in the eastern strait after disabling their radar. UKMTO separately reported a vessel hit by an unidentified projectile near Ras Al-Khaimah on Wednesday, causing an engine-room fire. Reuters could not verify Iran's account. At least 10 ships were hit in the first 10 days of November, after 37 attacks in October, per Washington Institute data.
items.headline: Four tankers struck by explosions in the Strait, Iran says

hormuz.stats: Traffic & shares (latest verified): AIS-visible commercial traffic is running about 8% of normal — 6.9 ships a day over the past week (18 tankers) against 84.8 before the crisis. EIA puts Hormuz oil flows at 4.9M bbl/day in Q2 2026, down from 21.6M in Q4 2025; the IEA estimates ~20M bbl/day transited in 2025, about a quarter of global seaborne oil trade. China takes ~42% and India ~13% of strait crude throughput; ~90% of Iran's oil exports go to China. The EIA warns vessel-tracking data have become less reliable during the conflict.

space.body: SpaceX's Starship Flight 15 is set to launch from Starbase in South Texas on Friday with a 75-minute window opening at 5:45 p.m. EDT, attempting to catch both the Super Heavy booster and the Ship upper stage — a first. The Ship will deploy 26 Starlink V3 satellites and circle Earth about 14 times over more than 22 hours before a possible catch the next day. ULA's Vulcan Centaur also returns to flight Friday, its first launch since February.
space.headline: Starship Flight 15 lifts off today in first attempt to catch both stages

space.body: SpaceX plans to retire Falcon 9, the rocket that carries the Dragon capsule — currently the only American spacecraft able to ferry NASA astronauts to the International Space Station — as Starship advances, and NASA has booked only three more Dragon flights, which would end in 2028. No further flights are booked beyond that point, leaving open how American astronauts will reach the station before it is retired in 2030; the next Starliner test flight is planned for this winter, with a crewed flight in 2028.
space.headline: Starship's rise leaves NASA's station trips in doubt after 2028

space.body: Scientists at UT Austin and Zhejiang University built a molecularly woven fabric that absorbed 97.9% of the benzene from a 50-50 benzene-cyclohexane mixture, a step toward far less energy-intensive separation of industrial chemicals used in nylon, paint, foams and detergents. Published in Nature, the work was co-authored by the late Nobel laureate Sir Fraser Stoddart.
space.headline: Reusable molecular fabric filters 97.9% of benzene from industrial mix

weekInBrief.body: Goldman Sachs strategists led by Peter Oppenheimer expect the S&P 500 to reach 8,700 over the next 12 months, a roughly 14% gain, arguing the recent selloff in megacap tech has left valuations attractive even as earnings growth slows from 36% this year to about 11% in 2027. The bank is overweight US and Japanese equities for 2027 and expects the bull market to continue as inflation, bond yields and oil prices moderate.
weekInBrief.headline: Goldman Sachs sees S&P 500 at 8,700 in 12 months, up 14%

weekInBrief.body: Crude has fallen roughly 20% from its late-October peak near $118 a barrel as hopes of de-escalation and rebounding flows through the Strait of Hormuz weigh on prices; the IEA says global oil supply exceeded demand by almost 2 million barrels a day in October, the first clear surplus since the US-Iran war began. Brent settled Thursday at $95.77, up 3.2% on the day after the latest tanker attacks.
weekInBrief.headline: Oil down about 20% from its October peak as supply outruns demand

weekInBrief.body: US existing-home sales fell 5.5% in October to a 3.75 million annual rate, the lowest since August 2010 and 8.8% below a year earlier, as the average 30-year mortgage rate averaged 7.33% in October. Inventory rose 1.3% to 1.59 million homes, or 5.1 months of supply, while the median price edged up 0.4% to $416,700.
weekInBrief.headline: Existing-home sales fall to a 16-year low as mortgage rates bite

weekInBrief.body: After a hotter-than-expected October CPI and a 6.5% annual PPI reading, CME FedWatch shows markets pricing a 100% likelihood of a Federal Reserve rate hike at the December meeting. October CPI rose 0.4% on the month, and the Fed's next decision comes Dec 8–9, with minutes from the October meeting due Nov 18.
weekInBrief.headline: Markets now fully price a December Fed rate hike
